definition: Neuroph is an object-oriented artificial neural network framework written in Java.
details: It can be used to create and train neural networks in Java programs. Neuroph provides Java class library as well as GUI tool easyNeurons for creating and training neural networks. It is an open-source project hosted at SourceForge under the Apache License. Versions before 2.4 were licensed under LGPL 3, from this version the license is Apache 2.0 License.

explainer.lead: Neuroph is a Java framework for building and training neural networks, giving Java developers a native library rather than a foreign-language dependency. It matters because it lowers the barrier to embedding neural networks directly in Java software.

tiers.eli5: It's a toolbox made for one programming language, so people who build with that language don't need to switch tools to add a small thinking machine to their program.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers construct and train networks through the Java class library or the easyNeurons GUI, and a pitfall is assuming old code snippets match the current license, since the project moved from LGPL 3 to Apache 2.0 at version 2.4.
tiers.paperLevel: Neuroph is an object-oriented artificial neural network framework written in Java, distributed as an open-source class library plus the easyNeurons graphical tool; it is hosted at SourceForge, under LGPL 3 before version 2.4 and Apache 2.0 from 2.4 onward.

explainer.example: A Java application adds the Neuroph library, defines a network in code or in easyNeurons, and trains it on its own data before shipping.
